newsitem.title: INDIA: India ports regulator to be announced this week.
newsitem.headline: India ports regulator to be announced this week.

text.p: The Indian government will announce the constitution of a regulatory authority for ports later this week, a senior government official said on Wednesday.
"The chairman and members would be notified in a day or two," S. Sundar, the highest-ranking civil servant in the Surface Transport Ministry, told a seminar on ports and roads in the Indian capital.
The regulator would fix and revise charges that can be levied by firms offering port services, which India opened up to private investors under an economic reform programme launched in 1991.
The Indian cabinet formally approved a proposal to constitute the authority earlier this year.
The first major port contract was awarded in January to a consortium led by Australia's P&O to build two berths in a new container terminal at the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust (JNPT) near Bombay.
Malaysia's Konsortium Perkaplan Berhad and India's DBC Port Management Private Ltd were the other members of the team.
The build-operate-transfer (BOT) contract involves an investment of between $200 million and $250 million, according to Indian officials.
The Indian government plans to award more such contracts to private firms.
Sundar said the JNPT contract was awarded in a transparent manner that satisified the bidders.
"Two of the four bidders who lost wrote to say that while they were disappointed they could not win the contract, they were pleased with the manner in which it was conducted," Sundar said.
